text:
Alex: Pushed a new attention benchmark run comparing kernel choices across A100 / H100 / L40S. Seq lenses: 128, 512, 2048, 8192. Batches: 1, 4, 16. Raw logs + flamegraphs in the build artifact: https://ci.redwood/attn-runs/1716002345
Priya: Nice, did you toggle the kernel-selector thresholds or run with the selector disabled?
Alex: Ran both. selector=on (default heuristics) and selector=off (force flash / force fused). The H100 regression shows up only with selector=on and H100+seq=8192+bsz=1.
Connor: Short tl;dr? numbers?
perf-bot: SUMMARY: A100 baseline (seq=8192 bsz=1) = 98 ms/token. H100 selector=on = 115 ms/token (+17%). H100 selector=off (force-fused-paged) = 96 ms/token (-1% vs A100). L40S similar to A100 within noise. KV-cache warm path unaffected.
Jian: That suggests kernel-selector picked a suboptimal kernel variant for that code-path on H100 at long seqs. Could be kernel launch overhead or an unexpected memcopy pattern.
Priya: Do we have nvprof/cupti traces? Any CUDA stall reasons (memcpy, sync, occupancy)?
Alex: Attached small profile snippets. Key line from nvprof: 
```
Kernel: flash_variant_X  time=48.1ms  achieved_occupancy=0.42  stalled_reason=memory_throughput
Kernel: fused_paged_Y   time=36.9ms  achieved_occupancy=0.78  stalled_reason=warp_exec
```
Alex: So selector picked flash_variant_X on H100 — high memory_throughput stalls. forcing fused_paged_Y fixes it.
Connor: Weird, we tuned flash_variant for large seqs specifically. Maybe its internal tiling favors SM layout on A100 but hurts on H100 because of L2 / HBW behavior.
Priya: Can you repro with isolated microbench? run `./build/bench_attn --device=h100 --kernel-selector=on --seq=8192 --bsz=1 --iters=20` and `--kernel-selector=off --kernel=fused_paged_Y`?
Alex: Ran both, paste of the run: 
```
# selector=on
iter times (ms): 118,116,115,114,117  mean=116.0
# selector=off (force fused_paged_Y)
iter times (ms): 97,96,95,96,94   mean=95.6
```
Jian: Did you collect hw counters? L2, DRAM throughput?
Alex: Yes — DRAM read throughput jumps ~1.4x under flash_variant_X on H100. L2 hit rate drops ~12%. On A100 the same variant shows higher L2 hit rate.
Priya: Could be our tiling/stride for KV cache prefetch doesn't match H100 L2 behavior. Maybe the ptx schedule or tensor core tiling differs.
Connor: Another angle: selector heuristics use a simple cost model based on seq*bsz and peak_mem estimate. At seq=8192, bsz=1 the memory working set touches a region that triggers a different code path (e.g., split attention vs paged). Perhaps our cost model uses A100-tuned constants.
Alex: Yep. I instrumented the selector decision table: for (seq>=4096 && bsz<=2) => choose flash_variant_X on all GPUs currently. That rule was added back in 2024 to prefer minimal kernel launches. It didn't consider per-GPU memory throughput.
perf-bot: NOTE: Canary rollout 2025-06-12 toggled that rule onto default fleet (80% traffic).
Priya: Action: we should make the selector consult a hardware profile (A100/H100/L40S) and fallback to fused_paged for H100 when seq>4096 & bsz<=2. Also we should add a microbench-based autotune to populate constants.
Connor: Agreed. Also add a quick perf regression test in CI: run the seq=8192 bsz=1 H100 microbench and assert mean <= 1.1x A100 baseline.
Jian: I'll take ownership of adding the hardware profile table. Alex can add the CI microbench and the rule change. Priya will validate the perf counters and create an instrumentation PR for the selector cost model.
Alex: Created PR #3821 with selector change (feature flag: attn.selector.hw_profiles). CI job added: perf/attn/seq8192-h100.
Priya: After PR lands, let's run a small fleet canary: selector.hw_profiles=on on h100-only pool and monitor latency p50/p95 and DRAM throughput.
Connor: One more note — KV cache eviction behavior: when forcing fused_paged_Y, KV cache eviction rate increases slightly for batch=16 at seq>=2048 (because fused path keeps more in-register state). Not a blocker but worth noting.
Alex: Logged a follow-up issue: EXT-1179 "KV eviction delta for fused_paged kernel at mid-large batches".
perf-bot: ARTIFACTS: https://ci.redwood/attn-runs/1716002345/artifacts (flamegraphs, nvprof, per-iter csv)
Priya: Cool. Plan for next 48h: Jian - hw profile table + tests, Alex - land selector PR + CI microbench, Connor - check memory allocator flags (pinned pages) in fused path. I'll validate counters and run fleet canary once PR is merged.
Alex: Thanks — will update thread with canary link when it's up.
Connor: :thumbsup:
Priya: :eyes:
